## Objective
- Expand Emberfall into a party-based RPG with deeper, balanced combat, status effects, achievements, and persistent rewards usable in later runs.

## Requirements
- Add a team, combat revives using a Phoenix Kit or similar, damage-over-time and elemental damage, control/confusion, and sleep.
- Add achievements and run rewards that persist and benefit future runs.
- Build the changes directly without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Planned a three-character party with one action per living member before each enemy turn.
- Planned per-run Spirit Shards, persistent achievements, and purchasable starting boons.
- Planned to retain the existing shop and tower-run structure while expanding combat.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a `partyRoster` container to `index.html`.
- Added a Legacy & Achievements panel and start-of-run Legacy Boons section to `index.html`.
- Added a run-reward message element to the game-over modal in `index.html`.

### Active
- Implement the party combat, Phoenix Kit revives, elemental/status skills, achievements, and persistent run progression.
- Add styling and test the complete playable game.

### Blocked
- A large attempted `game.js` rewrite failed because the tool input exceeded its limit; no replacement was applied.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current `index.html` edits and existing `game.js`.
2. Implement the game logic in smaller file-edit steps, including party turns, statuses, revives, achievements, and persistent boons.
3. Style the new party and legacy UI, then run available checks or play-test the browser game.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Partial UI additions for party roster, legacy/achievements, boons, and run rewards.
- `game.js`: Existing combat, run, shop, and persistence logic; major requested mechanics remain to be implemented.
- `combat.css`: Combat layout and responsive styles; needs party/status styling.
- `style.css`: Existing global styles for the game UI.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Existing game is a browser-based Emberfall tower-climber with three selectable classes and a between-floor shop.
- The `game.js` write attempt did not execute; the existing file remains unchanged.

## Objective
- Expand Emberfall into a party-based RPG with richer combat, persistent achievements, and rewards that improve future runs.

## Requirements
- Add a three-character team, Phoenix Kit revives, damage-over-time and elemental damage, control/confusion, and sleep.
- Add persistent achievements and purchasable starting boons.
- Retain the existing shop and tower-run structure; implement directly without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Each living party member gets one action before the enemy acts.
- Use per-run Spirit Shards, persistent achievements, and purchasable starting boons.
- Phoenix revival restores the first fallen party member to 40% vitality and consumes one kit.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added party combat, status skills/effects, Phoenix Kit revival, achievement/boon UI and purchase logic, and run-shard tracking.
- Added achievement triggers for first victory, sentinel defeat, level 3, Phoenix revival, and elemental/control skills.
- Added floor-clear shard rewards; accumulated run shards are deposited at game over.
- Fixed generic elemental/control skill validation so `classId: 'any'` skills can be used by every class.
- `node --check game.js` passed; captured a mobile Chromium screenshot showing the full class-selection and boon UI.

### Active
- Review combat turn/status handling and progression for remaining issues.
- Play-test combat, revival, rewards, persistence, and responsive layouts.
- Investigate party-member recovery between floors; current continue flow restores only the hero.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test combat actions, status durations, Phoenix revival, victory/game-over rewards, achievements, and boon purchases in-browser.
2. Check party recovery and shard handling when manually starting a new run.
3. Inspect responsive layouts beyond the initial mobile class-selection screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Party combat, statuses, achievements, boons, and run rewards.
- `index.html`: Party roster, legacy/achievement UI, and class selection with boon purchasing.
- `combat.css`: Combat layout, party roster, run-reward, and class-selection styling.
- `style.css`: Global styles plus legacy and boon styling.

## Important Context
- `game.js`, `index.html`, `combat.css`, and `style.css` have uncommitted changes.
- No interactive browser play-test has been run.
- Run-earned shards are banked at game over; achievement rewards are awarded immediately.
- `chooseClass()` gives Phoenix Kits only when the Phoenix boon is owned.
- Party members other than the hero do not currently regain vitality between floors.

- Each living party member gets one action before the enemy acts.
- Use per-run Spirit Shards, persistent achievements, and purchasable starting boons.
- Phoenix revival restores the first fallen party member to 40% vitality and consumes one kit.
- Between-floor recovery adds 30% maximum vitality to every party member, including fallen members.
- Bank unspent run shards when a player manually starts a new run.

- Added party combat, status skills/effects, Phoenix Kit revival, achievement/boon UI and purchase logic, and run-shard tracking.

- `game.js`: Party combat, statuses, achievements, boons, party recovery, and run rewards.
- `index.html`: Party roster, legacy/achievement UI, and class selection with boon purchasing.
- `combat.css`: Combat layout, party roster, run-reward, and class-selection styling.
- `style.css`: Global styles plus legacy and boon styling.

## Objective
- Expand Emberfall into a party-based RPG with richer combat, persistent achievements, and rewards that improve future runs.

## Requirements
- Add a three-character team, Phoenix Kit revives, damage-over-time and elemental damage, control/confusion, and sleep.
- Add persistent achievements and purchasable starting boons.
- Retain the existing shop and tower-run structure; implement directly without clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Each living party member gets one action before the enemy acts.
- Use per-run Spirit Shards, persistent achievements, and purchasable starting boons.
- Phoenix revival restores the first fallen party member to 40% vitality and consumes one kit.
- Between-floor recovery adds 30% maximum vitality to every party member, including fallen members.
- Bank unspent run shards when a player manually starts a new run.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented party combat, statuses and skills, Phoenix Kit revival, achievement/boon UI and purchases, run-shard tracking, floor recovery, and sentinel rewards.
- Smoke-tested Mage selection, party turn order, poison damage/duration, and persistent elemental achievement.
- Verified winning a floor awards one run shard; manual reset banks it once, alongside the First Blood reward, and a second reset does not duplicate shards.
- Verified boon purchase and achievement state persist across reloads.
- Tested Frost, Venom, Confounding Hex, and Lull; observed chill weakening damage, poison damage/duration, confusion self-damage, and sleep skipping an enemy turn.
- Checked responsive width at 320, 390, 768, 1024, and 1440 pixels; no horizontal overflow.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Verify game-over shard banking and duplicate-banking behavior.
- Verify Phoenix revival in combat and inspect remaining shop/combat layouts.

- (none)

1. Run `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-gameover.cjs` and confirm game-over reward banking and retry behavior.
2. Test Phoenix revival and confirm the kit is consumed and the first fallen member returns at 40% vitality.
3. Review any remaining layout or combat issues; rerun checks after changes.

## Relevant Files
- `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-gameover.cjs`: Prepared but not yet run; tests game-over banking.
- `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-status-layout.cjs`: Status-effect and responsive-width regression script.
- `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-regression.cjs`: Floor-clear banking and boon persistence test.
- `/tmp/opencode/emberfall-smoke.cjs`: Earlier browser smoke test.

## Important Context
- `game.js`, `index.html`, `combat.css`, and `style.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The floor-clear test ended with 4 shards: 1 run shard plus 3 from First Blood; a second reset left the total unchanged.
- The last browser test left the page at the class-selection screen with zero shards and no boons.
